items.text: The 15 skilled-trade jobs where you could earn a huge six-figure salary... without a college degree
items.article: America is short around 300,000 skilled-trade workers, and demand for maintenance technicians, electricians and plumbers will surge over the coming years. America has a skilled-worker problem – and it could be a golden opportunity for job seekers who are willing to get their hands dirty. Home Builders Institute President and CEO Ed Brady has warned that the country is short around 300,000 skilled-trade workers, leaving crucial jobs unfilled as the US races to build more homes, roads and bridges. Speaking to Fox Business this week, Brady said the shortage was being felt across trades like plumbing, electrical and painting. He warned that the explosion in data-center construction has only compounded the problem. 'Skilled trades' might conjure up images of hard hats and tool belts, but the market is considerably broader than that – stretching from aircraft maintenance and elevator repair to medical imaging and hospital facilities. Brady said many of these careers can offer six-figure earning potential without requiring a traditional four-year college degree , with some workers able to start earning around $30 an hour after high school and build from there. That does not mean every worker will immediately start out earning $100,000.
